name: Kullu Trout
subtitle: whole river trout crisped in mustard oil with ajwain and a hard squeeze of lemon

ingredients.qty: 2 whole trout, about 300g each, cleaned and slashed 3 times a side
ingredients.note: catalogued simply as fish — use trout, or any firm river fish
carom is the hill cook's fish spice; it cuts the oiliness

ingredients.qty: 1, half juiced and half in wedges

ingredients.note: a light dusting for extra crust

prepNotes: Pat the fish bone dry inside and out with kitchen paper. Any surface water and the marinade slides off and the skin steams instead of crisping.
Marinate 20 minutes only. Lemon juice on a delicate river fish for longer than that starts to cure the flesh and it goes chalky.
Bring the fish to room temperature before it hits the pan.

steps.text: Mix the turmeric, kashmiri chilli, chilli powder, ajwain, black pepper, ginger, garlic, lemon juice and salt into a thick paste.
Rub the paste over the fish and well into the slashes and the cavity. Rest 20 minutes.
steps.tip: Push it into the cuts with your fingers — that is the only way seasoning reaches the flesh of a whole fish.

steps.text: Dust each fish lightly with rice flour on both sides and shake off the excess.
Heat the mustard oil on a heavy tawa until it smokes, then cut the heat to medium for a minute.
Lay the fish in away from you and fry undisturbed for 5 minutes.
steps.tip: Do not poke it. The skin releases from the pan by itself when the crust has formed.

steps.text: Turn once with a wide spatula and fry the second side 4-5 minutes until the thickest part flakes at a fork.
Lift onto a warm plate, rest 2 minutes, scatter coriander and serve with lemon wedges and hot rice.

storage: Best eaten within the hour — the crust softens fast. Leftovers keep 1 day refrigerated; flake the cold flesh into a salad rather than reheating.
